newsitem.title: USA: Congress urged to regulate Indian casinos.
newsitem.headline: Congress urged to regulate Indian casinos.

text.p: The Justice Department urged Congress Wednesday to increase federal regulation of casinos run by Indian tribes and won the support of key senators.

Deputy Assistant Attorney Attorney General Kevin Di Gregory told the Senate Indian Affairs Committe that current laws left regulation of Indian casinos to the tribes and the 26 states where they are legal.

"There is a wide variation, however, in the regulatory systems in Indian gaming, and it is possible that in some instances neither the state nor the tribe would develop adequate regulation," Di Gregory said.
"Accordingly, there is a need for minimun federal regulatory standards for class III (casino) Indian gaming, which should be developed in consultation with tribal governments," he said.

Di Gregory said minimum federal standards were needed on background investigations and licensing of key casino managers and employees, credit and banking requirements, internal financial controls and surveillance and security systems.
Federal standards were backed by Committee Chairman John McCain, R-Arizona, Sen. Daniel Inouye of Hawaii, the panel's senior Democrat and Sen. Harry Reid, a Nevada Democrat.

"Today's hearing and the committee's previous hearing have provided an ample record to support moving, in the next Congress, legislation that establishes enforceable minimum federal standards," McCain said. He said opposition from the states had blocked the legislation this year.
"We are not far away from a major criminal scandal occurring at a tribal casino," Reid added.

The three members of the National Indian Gaming Commission and the chairman of the National Indian Gaming Association also endorsed minimum federal standards at tribal casinos, which are competing with private casinos for gambling revenue.
